Current Draft Statement/Design: One binary immune_activation_composite = OR(IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-α).
Scientific Correction: Keep cytokine-specific outputs and receptor/pathway-specific multi-label targets (at minimum TLR7, TLR8, TLR9; IFN-α, TNF-α, IL-6), with an overall composite only as a secondary derived field.
Why It Matters: IFN-α/TLR7 and IL-6/TNF/TLR8 can diverge within the same sequence; CpG classes also produce distinct profiles.
Required Action: Redesign y labels before final model training.

Current Draft Statement/Design: POS/NEG described as if it were the authors' published thresholded call.
Scientific Correction: Mark binary calls as curator-derived unless the source explicitly defines them. Preserve raw/continuous cytokine values, units, fold change, statistical significance, author interpretation, and the team's adjudication separately.
Why It Matters: Many papers report curves/continuous cytokines rather than a universal binary cutoff.
Required Action: Rebuild provenance fields and relabel existing rows.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Fixed rules such as IL-6 >2× or >200 pg/mL, TNF >100 pg/mL, IFN-α >50 pg/mL are presented as general label rules.
Scientific Correction: Do not use universal cytokine cutoffs unless validated. Store source-specific thresholds; for Burel-like ASO screening, use benchmark-relative ranking versus known clinical controls.
Why It Matters: Burel explicitly relies on relative ranking to ISIS104838/ISIS353512 and donor discrimination, not a universal pg/mL threshold.
Required Action: Remove unsupported universal thresholds; document adjudication method per study.

Scientific Correction: Primary evidence unit should be oligo × chemistry × strand state × dose × time × donor/cell system × delivery condition × endpoint. Derive an oligo-level summary only afterward.
Why It Matters: Same sequence can change phenotype by carrier, ss/duplex state, cell system and dose.

Scientific Correction: Remove as universal rules. 2'OMe effect depends on nucleotide identity, exact position, strand, sequence and receptor. A single 2'OMe-G can suppress TLR7 while preserving TLR8.
Why It Matters: A global percentage discards the position-specific biology.
Required Action: Replace with interaction features and receptor-specific outcomes.

Scientific Correction: Replace with: LNA effects on TLR9 are sequence- and context-dependent and can increase, decrease or leave activity unchanged.
Why It Matters: Riera-Tur directly shows opposite LNA effects across sequence series.
Required Action: Remove binary is_LNA causal conclusion; encode exact LNA positions and interactions.

Scientific Correction: Replace with: CpG methylation can reduce TLR9 activity in some contexts but is not sufficient; in an LNA context it can even increase TLR9 activation. Full cytosine methylation was more robust in several tested series.
Why It Matters: CpG presence/methylation is neither necessary nor sufficient for TLR9 phenotype.
Required Action: Recalculate CpG/methylation features and revise report conclusions.

Current Draft Statement/Design: ‘CpG in a DNA gap ≥14 nt is dangerous.’
Scientific Correction: Burel supports unmodified PS gap length as a risk contributor, but ISIS353512 is a non-CpG inflammatory ASO. Correct claim: longer unmodified PS gaps plus sequence context can raise human TLR9-like inflammatory risk independently of canonical CpG.
Why It Matters: Current wording incorrectly makes CpG part of the mechanism demonstrated by the key clinical case.
Required Action: Rewrite mechanism statement and feature interpretation.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Non-stimulatory sequences are treated as NEG/safe.
Scientific Correction: Separate inert/non-stimulatory from active antagonists and potentiators. Add immunomodulatory_direction = agonist | antagonist | potentiator | inert | mixed.
Why It Matters: 2'OMe RNAs and inhibitory ODNs can actively suppress TLR pathways.
Required Action: Relabel antagonist rows; exclude from simple NEG class.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Carrier, anticoagulant and cell system are not treated as core predictors/confounders.
Scientific Correction: Add delivery agent/formulation, whole blood vs PBMC, anticoagulant, fresh/frozen/rested status, cell subset and donor metadata.
Why It Matters: Heparin/EDTA can disrupt oligo-carrier complexes; whole blood vs PBMC profiles differ; fresh PBMC status is critical.
Required Action: Add schema fields and stratify analyses.

Current Draft Statement/Design: ‘PBMC pooled from multiple donors’ is used as a generic description.
Scientific Correction: Record whether donors were individual, pooled or averaged; keep donor-level IDs where available and donor phenotype/class where relevant.
Why It Matters: Burel identifies discriminator vs nondiscriminator donors and strong inter-donor variability.

Current Draft Statement/Design: 2'F is treated as a single protective effect and the cross-paper variation as an unresolved inconsistency.
Scientific Correction: Model 2'F by modified base, strand and position. Some 2'F-U examples suppress; 2'F-A is especially effective in Fucini; a single 2'F-G in Jung does not suppress TLR7/8.
Why It Matters: The apparent inconsistency is partly expected context dependence, not necessarily irreproducibility.
Required Action: Replace broad 2'F feature with position/base-resolved features.

Current Draft Statement/Design: High random/held-out AUC (~0.94) is described as clinically relevant proof while LOPO is ~0.65.
Scientific Correction: Treat the high AUC as preliminary internal performance. Report LOPO prominently and add grouped splits by paper, oligo family/near-neighbor sequence, and experimental series with confidence intervals.
Why It Matters: Near-neighbor sequences and laboratory-specific assay context can leak into random splits.
Required Action: Re-run evaluation with grouped/clustered splitting before scientific sign-off.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Sequence composition + coarse chemistry flags dominate.
Scientific Correction: Add strand-specific U count, positional bases, duplex ΔG/hybridization, overhang chemistry, 5' triphosphate, ss/duplex status, exact modification positions, gap length, palindrome/structure and carrier variables.
Why It Matters: These variables are experimentally linked to immune response.
Required Action: Expand feature engineering and data dictionary.

Current Draft Statement/Design: In-vitro fold-change bins are proposed to map to CTCAE grade.
Scientific Correction: Do not label in-vitro cytokine fold-change bins as CTCAE grades. If an ordinal response scale is used, call it experimental response severity unless clinically validated.
Why It Matters: The uploaded papers do not establish a direct CTCAE mapping.
Required Action: Remove CTCAE terminology from in-vitro ordinal model.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Synthetic polyT/polyGC rows are described as unambiguous NEG anchors without a primary assay source.
Scientific Correction: Only use a control as a training observation when its sequence, chemistry, assay and measured outcome are sourced. Proposed/synthetic controls may be kept in a separate design table.
Why It Matters: A negative control is assay-context dependent; some non-CpG/control ODNs show activity at high concentrations.
Required Action: Move unsourced controls out of training rows.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Several citations/identifiers are wrong or mismatched.
Scientific Correction: Correct DOI/PMID metadata and file identity before public release.
Why It Matters: Traceability is a Phase 2 quality requirement.
Supporting Papers: Riera-Tur 2024; Fucini 2012; Goodchild 2009; Lenert 2010; uploaded 'Hornung 2005' file
Required Action: Apply citation corrections in Citation_QC sheet.

Current Draft Statement/Design: Draft is framed as immunotoxicity broadly but largely models TLR7/8/9.
Scientific Correction: Either explicitly scope v1 as endosomal nucleic-acid-sensor immunostimulation or add separate labels/features for RIG-I/MDA5/TLR3/cGAS when evidence is available.
Why It Matters: Different receptor classes have different structural triggers and assay contexts.
Required Action: Define scope in title/methods and avoid pathway overclaim.
